task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of August 12, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style newspaper news update on the Pine Estuary Journal's printing move, including what readers, advertisers and print workers will notice.

facts.text: The Pine Estuary Journal announced Wednesday, Aug. 12, 2026, that its weekday editions will be printed at Oriole Pressworks beginning Oct. 5.
The contracted printer is 62 miles from the newspaper's current pressroom.
Publisher Veda Quill said the newspaper will continue publishing five print editions a week and will not change its subscription price at the move.
The newspaper's weekday print deadline will move from 10:30 p.m. to 8:30 p.m. to allow transport time.
Late council meetings and evening sports results may appear online first and in the next print edition whose deadline has not passed.
Delivery contractors have been given the same target doorstep times as under the existing printing arrangement.
The company has not completed a trial run of the new weekday transport route.
The current pressroom employs nine people; three have accepted packaging jobs at the Journal and six positions will be eliminated.
The six affected employees have been offered severance based on service length; individual amounts were not disclosed.
The newspaper will retain its newsroom, advertising staff and public office in Pine Estuary.
Quill estimates $380,000 in recurring annual printing and maintenance savings once the move is complete; one-time transition expenses are separate and their total was not disclosed.
The existing press needs a replacement control unit, quoted by the publisher at a one-time $240,000; that is not an annual maintenance cost.
Commercial leaflets currently printed for local shops will also move to the contractor; order deadlines for those jobs are still being negotiated.
Press operator Deni Vale said, "We know which rollers complain before the machine stops. That knowledge does not fit in a moving box."
Hardware advertiser Kira Stenn said she needs confirmation of the leaflet deadline before booking her November sale.
Editor Milo Reeve said the newsroom plans an online late-news page but has not announced a paid-access change.
Reeve said, "An earlier press time changes when a reader gets a fact, not whether we should report it."
The Journal's current print circulation is 11,200, according to its latest publisher statement, not an independently audited figure in this packet.
The newspaper installed its current press in 1993 and still prints a weekly tide table on the back page.
No decision has been announced about selling the pressroom property or changing the newspaper's ownership.

forbidden_additions: A reduction in print publication days or a confirmed on-time transport trial
A property sale, ownership change or independently audited circulation absent from the record
